messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather data for tomorrow at a location ?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content: Sure! To pull tomorrow’s forecast I’ll need the latitude and longitude of the spot you’re interested in. Could you share those coordinates (or a city name that I can look up)? Once I have the location, I’ll fetch the weather data for tomorrow.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Can you retrieve the weather data for tomorrow at a location?" They didn't specify a location. We need to ask for location details: latitude, longitude, maybe city. Also we need to ask for date? They want tomorrow. So we can ask for location. Then we can call the function to get weather data. The function requires latitude and longitude. We can ask for them. Also we might need to specify timezone? The API may return forecast. We can use the open-meteo API. The function signature includes params: latitude, longitude, elevation. We can set elevation null. We need to call the function with the URL. The URL likely is something like "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to include query parameters: latitude, longitude, hourly=temperature_2m, daily=weathercode, etc. But the function signature only includes latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't allow specifying other query parameters. So maybe the function is simplified. But we can still call it with those parameters. The function will return whatever the API returns. We can then parse the data. But we need to ask for location first.

Thus respond: "Sure, could you provide the latitude and longitude of the location?" Or ask for city name and we can convert to lat/lon. But we don't have geocoding. So ask for lat/lon. Also ask for timezone? But not needed.

Thus answer: ask for location.
